2026-08-07T12:32:17.6245718Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6246140Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6246652Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6247221Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6247671Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6248267Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6250195Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6252350Z >
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6255193Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6258387Z >
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6259294Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6260216Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6260396Z ### How to Use
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6260639Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6261404Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6262251Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6262421Z ```bash
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6262976Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6263789Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6264464Z ```
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6264669Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6264981Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6265559Z ```bash
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6266140Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6267241Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6268220Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6269062Z ```
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6269275Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6269991Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6270997Z ```bash
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6271607Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6272380Z ```
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6272591Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6272929Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6273767Z ```bash
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6274342Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6275347Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6276136Z ```
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6276337Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6276808Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6277295Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6279050Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6281036Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6281208Z ```bash
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6281677Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6282643Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6283590Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6283935Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6284463Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6285621Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6287454Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6289574Z ```
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6289821Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6290761Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6292016Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6292194Z ```bash
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6293014Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6294072Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6294889Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6295387Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6295843Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6297013Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6297617Z ```
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6297829Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6298058Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6298972Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6300102Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6301228Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6302401Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6303705Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6304349Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6304527Z ### Notes
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6304749Z 
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6305492Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6307419Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6308916Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6310401Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6311827Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6313122Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6314262Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-07T12:32:17.6315077Z </mcp-clis>
